chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, or someone else, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, who said:

I performed Hajj with my father, and with me was a sister of mine. So when we arrived in Makkah, she menstruated, and she panicked with an intense panic, fearing that the Hajj would be missed by her. So my father said to me, 'Go to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and say to him that my father conveys the greeting to you, and says to you that a young girl of mine, whom I am performing Hajj with, has menstruated and panicked with an intense panic, fearing that the Hajj would be missed by her. So what are your orders for her?'
He said, 'So I went to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he was in the Sacred Masjid. So I stood by his side. So when he looked at me, he gestured to me. So I went to him and said to him,

He said, 'So I returned to my father and conveyed it to him. He said, 'So he instructed her with that, and she did so, and the blood was cut off from her, and she fulfilled all of the rituals. So when she departed from Makkah after the Hajj, and came to be in the carriage, the blood returned to her.'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ): Abu Al-Hasan (AS), referring to Imam Al-Hasan (AS)
key_terms.فَلْتَسْتَدْخِلْهَا: Let her insert it inside (her body)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for a woman who menstruates during Hajj and wants to complete her rituals?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the concept of *istidkhal* (internal tamponade) using milk-soaked cotton, a practical juristic solution to ensure the validity of Hajj rituals despite menstruation. It highlights the Imam’s authority in providing specific medical-legal remedies that allow a pilgrim to perform all rites, emphasizing the Shia scholarly focus on facilitating religious obligations through tangible means. The narrative underscores the importance of timely action and the specific conditions under which menstruation is considered to have ceased for ritual purity purposes.
